extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of literature; novelists and critics
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Lukács' philosophical-historical criteria for judging the novel as a form: classify novel type, assess hero/world relations, stance of irony, temporal handling, and metaphysical honesty relative to the historical situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for the novel as form
rubrics_metrics.description: The novel becomes the necessary form when: the world has lost its sense of immanent meaning; the individual is the carrier of value (no transcendent authority); time is felt as duration rather than as eternity; irony becomes the only stance commensurate with the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this cluster of historical-philosophical conditions to judge whether a work properly belongs to the novel form rather than older forms (e.g., epic). Anti-pattern: treating the novel as merely a looser epic without attending to the changed experience of meaning, individuality, and temporality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type: Abstract Idealism (Don Quixote)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemplar: Don Quixote. The hero possesses an interiority that demands the world conform to its ideals; the narrative tension is between 'a soul too narrow' for the wide world's complexity. Failure is heroic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify protagonists whose inward totalities attempt to remake reality and whose heroic failure is central. Consider whether the work presents the protagonist's ideals as worthy though untenable, rather than merely deluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type: Romanticism of Disillusionment (Flaubert)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exemplar: Flaubert's Sentimental Education. The hero possesses 'a soul too wide' for the world's narrowness; failure is melancholy rather than heroic. Interiority becomes contemplation; the novel records disenchantment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for protagonists whose breadth of sensibility or expectation exceeds social reality, producing melancholic or contemplative failure. Anti-pattern: reading every failure as heroic—distinguish melancholic resignation from heroic persistence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type: Hegelian Bildungsroman (synthesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goethe's Wilhelm Meister attempts a synthesis: the hero learns to 'adjust' ideals to the world. The world is partially redeemed; the soul partially compromises. This is a rare third option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the novel stages a negotiated reconciliation between individual and world rather than absolute failure or uncompromising idealism. Rarity of this synthesis is itself a critical point—note whether reconciliation is convincing or merely formal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation between hero and world
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze the relation between hero and world along the axes 'too narrow soul' / 'too wide soul' / 'mutual adjustment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This dimension is a primary classificatory tool: map characters' interiority against social reality. Use it to determine type (idealism, disillusionment, Bildung) and to judge the novel's formal coherence with its historical situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irony as the novelist's stance
rubrics_metrics.description: Irony is the formal name for simultaneously holding that the novelist cannot affirm the world (it refuses to be epic) and cannot affirm the soul (the soul fails to remake the world).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the narrative voice, structure, and tone enact this double negation—do they retain critical distance and recognition of limits? Anti-pattern: sentimentalizing or uncritically affirming either world or soul, which undermines the novel's formal honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of time: epic eternity vs. lived duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the novel treats time as 'epic eternity' (timeless, total) or as 'duration'—the lived, historical flow characteristic of the modern novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine pacing, episodic structure, and historical embedding to determine temporal orientation. A proper novel registers duration and the historical temporal consciousness of its era; treating events as eternal or mythic may align it with epic tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of loss of immanent meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the novel acknowledges the loss of immanent meaning in the world or pretends that meaning remains intact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the work confronts modern disenchantment honestly. Anti-pattern: metaphysical dishonesty—technically skillful novels that nonetheless pretend a coherent, immanent world when social-historical conditions no longer permit this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual as carrier of value
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelic situation presumes the individual as the carrier of value in the absence of transcendent authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the degree to which the narrative centers individual subjective experience as the locus of value judgments, and whether that centering is critically interrogated or unproblematically affirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphysical honesty / appropriateness to historical situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Lukács asks not 'is it well-made?' but 'is it appropriate to the world it confronts?' A novel can be technically accomplished and metaphysically dishonest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as an overarching evaluative test: a technically excellent novel may still fail if it misrepresents the epochal relation between individual and world. Score works higher that demonstrate formal techniques aligned with an authentic grasp of their historical/contextual conditions.
